fullPassage: In music, proximity may refer to elements' being close together in pitch, time, or space. For example, notes that are similar in pitch may be grouped together. Notes are also grouped together if they are played together in time or if they come from the same instrument or section of a larger musical group. To get a sense of the idea of proximity, imagine a person playing a piano. Typically, the right hand plays notes that are higher in pitch than the left hand. Also, most often, it is the right hand that plays the melody, whereas the left hand plays the bass line or accompaniment. Even though all of the notes are played in close spatial proximity and at approximately the same time, we hear the notes from the right hand emerging as melody because they are grouped together with respect to pitch. Similarly, in some of Bach's famous solo music for violin, the violinist essentially creates two streams of music by simultaneously playing both high and lower notes. Perceptually, we group the high notes together and group the low notes together, so we hear it as polyphonic or as two lines of music.

questions.passage: In music, proximity may refer to elements' being close together in pitch, time, or space. For example, notes that are similar in pitch may be grouped together. Notes are also grouped together if they are played together in time or if they come from the same instrument or section of a larger musical group. To get a sense of the idea of proximity, imagine a person playing a piano. Typically, the right hand plays notes that are higher in pitch than the left hand. Also, most often, it is the right hand that plays the melody, whereas the left hand plays the bass line or accompaniment. Even though all of the notes are played in close spatial proximity and at approximately the same time, we hear the notes from the right hand emerging as melody because they are grouped together with respect to pitch. Similarly, in some of Bach's famous solo music for violin, the violinist essentially creates <u>two streams of music</u> by simultaneously playing both high and lower notes. Perceptually, we group the high notes together and group the low notes together, so we hear it as polyphonic or as two lines of music.
questions.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 two streams of music가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: two streams of music = 높은 음과 낮은 음이 분리 인식되는 두 갈래의 선율
det.analysis:
❌ ① 서로 다른 악기에서 나오는 악곡 (하나의 바이올린에서 나옴)

✅ ② 높은 음과 낮은 음이 분리 인식되는 두 갈래의 선율 (원문 'we group the high notes together and group the low notes together'와 일치) ← 정답

❌ ③ 활의 물리적 움직임이 만드는 소리 (물리적 움직임이 아닌 청각적 인식의 결과)

❌ ④ 의도적 화성 진행 패턴 (화성 진행이 아닌 음높이에 의한 청각적 그룹화)
det.tip: two streams = 높은 음 그룹 + 낮은 음 그룹 → 분리 인식
